question:
In a proton-capture process, the reaction $^{15}\!N + ^1\!H \rightarrow ^{16}\!O + \gamma$ occurs.

Given atomic masses: $M(^{15}\!N)=15.000109\,u$, $M(^1\!H)=1.007825\,u$, $M(^{16}\!O)=15.994915\,u$.
Also given: $m_n=1.008665\,u$ and $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$.

(a) Using mass–energy equivalence, calculate the $Q$-value of the reaction and state whether energy is released or absorbed.

(b) Neglecting recoil, estimate the energy of the emitted $\gamma$ photon.

(c) Using binding energy from atomic masses
\[\Delta m = Zm_H + (A-Z)m_n - M_{atom},\qquad BE=\Delta m\,c^2\]
compute $BE$ and $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ for $^{15}\!N$ and $^{16}\!O$.

(d) Evaluate how the change in $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ supports your conclusion about stability after the reaction.

options.A: $Q\approx +12.13\,\text{MeV}$ (released), $E_\gamma\approx 12.13\,\text{MeV}$, and $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ increases from $\approx 7.70$ to $\approx 7.98\,\text{MeV}$ so $^{16}\!O$ is more stable
options.B: $Q\approx -12.13\,\text{MeV}$ (absorbed), $E_\gamma\approx 12.13\,\text{MeV}$, and $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ increases so $^{15}\!N$ is more stable
options.C: $Q\approx +1.21\,\text{MeV}$ (released), $E_\gamma\approx 1.21\,\text{MeV}$, and $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ decreases so $^{16}\!O$ is less stable
options.D: $Q\approx +12.13\,\text{MeV}$ (released), $E_\gamma\approx 12.13\,\text{MeV}$, but $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)$ decreases from $\approx 7.98$ to $\approx 7.70\,\text{MeV}$ so $^{16}\!O$ is less stable
